basis: Neuroserpin inclusions cause progressive encephalopathy and dementia.
Mitochondrial energy disorder with defining neurodegeneration; reduced visual acuity and cardiac pre-excitation each occur in 2/3 patients.
Lipomatous mass occupies the spinal cord compartment; neurologic origin and dysraphism define the condition.
Ovarian carcinoma; pulmonary type describes morphology, not lung origin. No endocrine dysfunction is defining.
Nematode infection; migrating larvae directly cause subcutaneous inflammation in most patients. CNS, ocular and pulmonary invasion are minority manifestations.
Hydrocephalus and intellectual disability define the syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Hearing and optic nerve abnormalities occur in fewer than 30%.
Defining CNS hypomyelination and spasticity; optic disc pallor supports optic nerve damage in 3/10 patients, at the inclusion threshold.
Developmental disability defines the syndrome; strabismus and pectus excavatum each occur in 30-79%. GI symptoms lack clear evidence of direct organ damage.
Congenital absence of the cerebellar vermis is a structural CNS malformation.
Developmental disability and sparse hair define disease; kidney abnormalities occur in 30-79%, VSD in 3/8. Frequent contractures and foot deformities omitted at cap.
Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias with vertebral abnormalities; extra-skeletal disease is not shared across most subtypes.
Endocrine tumors define MEN4. Supplied HPO lists renal angiomyolipoma, pulmonary carcinoid and subcutaneous lipoma each at 30-79%; GI ulcers are separate diagnoses.
Congenital reduction and fusion of digits involve limb bones, joints, muscles, tendons and ligaments.
Proximal renal tubulopathy defines disease; developmental delay occurs in 3/4. Elevated CK and transaminases alone do not establish muscle or liver damage.
Peripheral corneal ulceration, typically representing immune-mediated marginal keratitis from hypersensitivity to bacterial antigens.
Absent T cells 1/1; respiratory distress 2/2, failure 1/1; cardiac malformations 1/1. Tethered cord, cleft palate and renal duplication omitted at cap; tiny series.
Progressive white-matter degeneration and ovarian endocrine failure define disease; ovarian insufficiency occurs in 5/6. Muscle enzyme changes alone do not prove myopathy.
Craniosynostosis, limb skeletal malformations and congenital heart disease are defining features.
Pituitary infarction or hemorrhage; visual field loss occurs in 80-99% from optic-pathway compression, and cranial nerve paralysis in 30-79%.
Benign neoplasms of skin and subcutaneous tissue define this integumentary umbrella; reproductive and breast subtypes add no axis.
Microcephaly and developmental delay define the originally described phenotype. [Original report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7509568/).
Mixed germ-cell and sex-cord tumor of reproductive gonads; endocrine dysfunction is not a defining manifestation.
Endolymphatic sac tumor originates in the inner ear; destructive invasion of adjacent petrous temporal bone is characteristic and common, exceeding 30%.
Definition specifies urate urinary stones; urinary tract disease does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Toxic injury causes myocardial inflammation; an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism is not established.
